exam: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
q: Which one of the following is an animal belonging to the Marsupial category?
explanation: The koala is a marsupial of Australia that carries its young in a pouch. Rabbit, porcupine and squirrel are placental mammals.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
q: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
explanation: Insects such as the grasshopper breathe through a network of tracheae opening at spiracles; gills and lungs belong to other animals.

exam: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
q: In which of the following arthropods is the first pair of legs on the cranial segment modified into pincer-like forcipules?
explanation: Centipedes (Chilopoda) have their first pair of trunk legs modified into poison claws called forcipules. Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment and no forcipules; cicadas and wasps are insects.

exam: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
q: What is the primary purpose of a Wasp's sting?
options: To defend themselves or their colony
key_text: To defend themselves or their colony
explanation:
Most books and keys: defence of self and colony. Strictly: in solitary wasps the sting is used mainly to paralyse prey (Britannica, "wasp").
Wasps chiefly use the sting (a modified ovipositor) to defend themselves and the colony. Solitary wasps also use it to paralyse prey, but stinging plays no part in pollination or marking territory.

exam: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
q: Why chameleon changes its colours?
options: To tune its colour with temperature of the day
The colours automatically change on their own
explanation:
Most books and keys: to protect itself from predators (camouflage). Strictly: chameleons change colour mainly for social signalling and thermoregulation (Stuart-Fox & Moussalli 2008, PLoS Biology).
Most books say chameleons change colour mainly to camouflage themselves against predators. Strictly, colour change serves mainly social signalling and temperature control.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Which among the following does not contain crop
explanation: The emu, a flightless ratite, has no crop. Turkey, duck and quail store food in a crop. (Off-topic: zoology.)

exam: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
q: Which of the following is NOT an example of class Amphibia?
explanation: Clarias is a catfish (class Pisces), not an amphibian. Bufo (toad), Rana (frog) and Hyla (tree frog) are amphibians. (Off-topic: zoology.)

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Which of the following enzyme is elevated in Downer cow syndrome
explanation: In downer cow syndrome the recumbent cow suffers muscle damage, so serum creatine phosphokinase (CK) rises sharply; tryptophan and creatinine are not enzymes.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
q: The foods of Protozoans is digested by
explanation: Protozoa such as Amoeba digest food with enzymes inside food vacuoles; contractile vacuoles remove water.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: The postmortem sample collected during abortion is
explanation: After an abortion the aborted fetus (with placenta) is the key post-mortem sample for diagnosing the cause; blood, milk or serum are ante-mortem samples.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: No. of lobes present in left lung of cow
explanation:
Most keys: 3 lobes (apical/cranial, cardiac/middle, diaphragmatic/caudal). Strictly in current veterinary nomenclature the left lung has 2 lobes, the cranial lobe being split into two parts (general knowledge, not checked).
Classical veterinary anatomy divides the ox's left lung into three lobes (apical, cardiac, diaphragmatic); the right lung has four or five.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Which of the following is not used in lactic acidosis in cattle
explanation: Rumen lactic acidosis is treated with alkalising agents - sodium bicarbonate, magnesium hydroxide, Ringer's lactate fluids; vinegar (acetic acid) is used for urea/ammonia poisoning, not acidosis.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Pneumatic bones are commonly present in
explanation: Birds have pneumatic (air-filled) bones that lighten the skeleton for flight; cattle, horses and pigs have solid marrow-filled bones.

exam: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
q: The venom of Russell's Viper primarily affects the
explanation: Russell's viper venom is haemotoxic: it disrupts blood clotting (consumption coagulopathy, bleeding). Cobra and krait venoms are the neurotoxic ones.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Paste consisting of the drug mixed with either honey/jaggery and administered orally in large animals is called
explanation: An electuary is a drug mixed into a paste with honey, jaggery or treacle and given by mouth (smeared on the tongue). A bolus is a large pill, a drench a liquid dose, a pessary a vaginal insert.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: The artery used for recording pulse in dog is
explanation: In dogs the pulse is recorded from the femoral artery on the inner thigh.

exam: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
q: Site of recording pulse in dogs
explanation: The pulse of a dog is taken at the femoral artery (inner thigh); the coccygeal artery is used in cattle and the jugular is a vein.

exam: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
q: Tracheal respiration occurs in which of the following organisms?
explanation: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
q: Identify the organisms that undergo cutaneous respiration.
explanation: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.

exam: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
q: What is the main function of worker bees in a hive?
explanation: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.

exam: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
q:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
options: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
key_text: Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
explanation: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
q: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
explanation: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

exam: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
q: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
explanation: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
q: What happens if you plug in a heater device rated for 110 V, 50 Hz in a household AC electric supply plug in India?
options: It burns out within minutes or even in seconds
Its heat supply would be poorer than its rated value.
You cannot use such a device in an Indian Plug
key_text: It burns out within minutes or even in seconds
explanation: On India's 230 V supply a 110 V heater draws about (230/110)² ≈ 4 times its rated power, so its element burns out quickly. Off-topic (physics).

exam: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
q: Under what conditions the resistivity of the material does not change?
options: When the shape of the resistor is changed
When both the material and temperature are changed
key_text: When the shape of the resistor is changed
explanation: Resistivity is a property of the material and its temperature, so it does not change when only the shape (length or area) of the resistor changes; resistance would change, resistivity would not.

exam: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
q: Which of the following is incorrect about the ultrasonic waves?
options: These waves are can be used for imaging
It cannot be heard by normal human ears
The speed of ultrasonic waves is more in denser media
The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
key_text: The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
explanation: Ultrasonic waves are mechanical sound waves and cannot travel through vacuum; they are inaudible, used for imaging and travel faster in denser media. Moved.

exam: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
q: The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour it
explanation: An opaque object looks the colour of the light it reflects; the other colours are absorbed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
q: When a semiconductor is heated, its resistance would
options: Resistance has no relation with temperature
explanation: A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient: heating frees more charge carriers, so its resistance decreases (a metal's would increase). Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
q: The electrical resistance of the insulators is
explanation: An ideal insulator offers (practically) infinitely high resistance to current, hence 'infinitely high' rather than merely 'high'. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
q: What is the cause of dispersion of light through a prism?
explanation: A prism disperses white light because each colour is refracted by a different amount. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: Twinkling of stars is due to?
explanation: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction by turbulent air layers of changing density. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
q: When there is a short circuit what happens to the current in the circuit?
explanation: In a short circuit resistance falls almost to zero, so the current increases heavily. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: An electric fuse is used to prevent?
explanation: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when an excessive (heavy) current flows, protecting appliances. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
q: At the time of short circuit, the current in the circuit
explanation: In a short circuit the resistance becomes almost zero, so the current rises very sharply (which blows the fuse). Physics, moved to book 5 row 1.

exam: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
q: Grass appears green because
explanation: Grass looks green because chlorophyll reflects green light and absorbs the rest. Off-topic (physics/biology), moved.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: What is the principle of working of transformer?
explanation: A transformer works on mutual induction: a changing current in the primary coil induces an emf in the secondary coil.

exam: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
q: Which of the following coloured lights has the highest wavelength?
explanation: Red light has the longest wavelength of visible light (about 620–750 nm); yellow, green and blue are progressively shorter.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: Which of the following is not a primary colour?
explanation: Red, green and blue are the additive primary colours of light, so yellow is not one. (Moved to 5:1.)

exam: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
q: What is the common name of Asafoetida (Ferula asafoetida) which is the dried sap or gum resin obtained from the roots of Ferula plants and used in several Indian dishes?
explanation: Asafoetida is hing, the dried gum-resin from the roots of Ferula. Methi is fenugreek, saunf fennel and ajwain carom seed.

exam: APPSC 2022 Assistant Conservator of Forest
q: What cooking methods involve a small amount of hot liquid, ideally at a temperature between 160 and 180F usually done with eggs, delicate grains and certain veggies?
explanation: Poaching cooks food gently in a small amount of hot liquid at about 160–180 °F, as for eggs. Blanching is a brief dip in boiling water, baking uses dry oven heat and broiling direct heat.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2010 (25-10-2010)
q: The chicory powder which is mixed with coffee is obtained from:
explanation: Chicory powder used as a coffee additive is made from the roasted roots of the chicory plant, not its stem, leaves or seeds.

exam: APPSC Group-II 2011
q: The colour of Cow's milk is slightly yellowish due to the presence of
explanation: Cow's milk is slightly yellow because of carotene (beta-carotene) in its fat; 'Carolin' is the paper's misprint of carotin (carotene). Riboflavin only gives whey a greenish-yellow tint, so the printed key (b) is wrong.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2004 (28-03-2004)
q: After parboiling, the nutritive value of rice
explanation: Parboiling drives water-soluble B vitamins and minerals from the husk and bran into the grain, so rice's nutritive value increases.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2010 (05-09-2010)
q: Lutein is a/an:
explanation: Lutein is a yellow xanthophyll pigment (marigold, egg yolk, the eye's macula). Blue/purple is anthocyanin, orange is carotene.

exam: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
q: Which is the most widely used method of cooking food?
explanation: Boiling is the most widely used cooking method in Indian homes (rice, dal, vegetables). Frying, barbecuing and tenderising are less common.

exam: APPSC 2012 Group-1
q: The percentage of water in milk is measured by
explanation: A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so its water content. A hygrometer measures humidity, a hydrometer liquid density in general.

exam: APPSC Group-1 PYQ
q: ' Oryza sativa ' is the scientific name of:
explanation: Oryza sativa is cultivated rice. Wheat is Triticum, maize Zea mays and potato Solanum tuberosum.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2003
q: With what is the banana plant propagated?
explanation: Banana is propagated vegetatively by suckers, the side shoots from the underground stem. Cultivated bananas are seedless, so seeds are not an option.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2003
q: Ginger is a kind of
explanation: Ginger is a rhizome, an underground stem that stores food, so of these options it is a tuberous stem. It is not a root.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2010 (25-10-2010)
q: Tomato belongs to family of:
explanation: Tomato belongs to Solanaceae, the same family as potato, brinjal and chilli. Gramineae is grasses, Leguminosae is pulses and Malvaceae is cotton and okra.

exam: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
q: The caramelization reactions require intense heat about
explanation: Caramelisation of sucrose needs about 170 °C (it begins near 160 °C); 100 °C only boils water and 200-240 °C burns the sugar.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: The pH value of Curd as compared to that of Milk would be?
explanation: Curd contains lactic acid formed by bacteria from lactose, so it is more acidic than milk and its pH is lower (about 4-4.5 against 6.5-6.7).

exam: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
q: Curd should not be kept in
explanation: Curd is acidic and reacts with brass (copper-zinc), forming toxic salts, so it should not be kept in brass vessels; glass, steel and earthen pots are safe.

exam: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
q: Which of the following is an example of a Maillard reaction?
options: Burning of eyes while cutting onions
explanation: The Maillard reaction is the browning of food when sugars react with amino acids on heating - e.g. bread turning into toast; tears from onions, egg hardening (protein denaturation) and curd formation are other processes.

exam: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
q:
Match
List-I with
List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:
List-1 (Physicists):
A. WK Roentgen
B. Victor Francis Hess
C. Ernest Orlando Lawrence
D. CH Townes
List-2 (Major contribution/discovery):
1. Cosmic radiation
2. Maser
3. X-rays
4. Cyclotron
explanation: Roentgen discovered X-rays, Hess cosmic radiation, Lawrence invented the cyclotron and Townes the maser, so A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2. Off-topic science, moved.

exam: APPSC Executive Officer Gr-III Endowment Paper-I General Stu
q:
Match the Name of Scientists in
List-I to their fields of expertise Subject in
List-II.
List-I:
A. Pier Antonio Micheli
B. George Cuvier
C. Rudolf Virchow
D. Stephen Hales
List-II: i. Plant physiology ii. Pathology iii. Palaeontology iv. Mycology
explanation: Micheli – mycology, Cuvier – palaeontology, Virchow – pathology, Stephen Hales – plant physiology. Off-topic, moved.

exam: APPSC Junior Lecturers, Polytechnic Lecturers Paper-I Genera
q:
Match
List I (Physical quantities) with
List II (Units) and choose the correct option:
List I:
I. Electric current
II. Temperature
III. Luminous Intensity
List II:
a. candela
b. ampere
c. kelvin
explanation: SI units: current – ampere, temperature – kelvin, luminous intensity – candela. Off-topic, moved.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
q: If Kilo is Thousand, then Deka is
explanation: Deka (deca) is the SI prefix for ten (10^1); kilo = 10^3, hecto = 10^2.

exam: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
q: Who among the following determined the charge of electrons as 1.5924 x 10^-19 C?
explanation: Robert Millikan's oil-drop experiment (1909-13) measured the electron's charge, about 1.59 x 10^-19 C in his 1913 result (now 1.602 x 10^-19 C).

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
q: Which instrument is used to measure speed?
explanation: A tachometer measures speed (rotational speed of an engine, rpm); an ammeter measures current, a venturimeter flow rate. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
q: A projector for images of both opaque objects and transparencies is called an ______.
explanation: An epidiascope projects images of both opaque objects and transparencies (episcope + diascope); an anemometer measures wind speed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
q: A hydrometer is used to measure?
explanation: A hydrometer measures the relative density (specific gravity) of liquids; humidity is measured by a hygrometer. Off-topic (physics), moved.

exam: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
q: Who among the following wrote 'De Magnete' in the 1600s, which gave the first rational explanation of the compass needle's mysterious ability to point north-south?
explanation: William Gilbert's De Magnete (1600) first explained the compass by treating the Earth as a giant magnet. Off-topic (physics), moved to book 5.

exam: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
q: In which year did John Dalton present his atomic theory?
explanation: John Dalton put forward his atomic theory in the early 1800s and published it in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' (1808), the year usually asked.

exam: APPSC Group-II 2008
q: The first synthetically prepared organic compound was
explanation: Friedrich Wohler synthesised urea from inorganic ammonium cyanate in 1828, the first organic compound made in a laboratory.

exam: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
q: Steridian is unit of?
explanation: The steradian is the SI unit of solid angle; the radian measures a plane angle.

exam: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
q: An electric bulb is rated 11 W. What does W signify here?
options: Amount of electricity consumed in a day
explanation: The watt is the unit of power, i.e. energy consumed per unit time (1 W = 1 J/s); an 11 W bulb uses 11 joules each second. It does not measure light output or daily consumption.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: According to Kohlberg, which is the highest stage of moral reasoning?
explanation: Kohlberg's sixth and highest stage is the 'universal ethical principle' orientation (post-conventional). Law and order is stage 4, social contract stage 5 and punishment-avoidance stage 1.

exam: APPSC Group-I Prelims 2004 (28-03-2004)
q: Where is the Black Box fitted in planes?
explanation: The black box (flight data and cockpit voice recorders) is fitted in the tail section, the part most likely to survive a crash.

exam: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
q: From environmental considerations, which of the following is a better option to serve Tea or trains?
options: Serving in glass cups or metal glasses, which are reusable
key_text: Serving in glass cups or metal glasses, which are reusable
explanation:
Printed key (APPSC): reusable glass or metal cups. Kulhads were also promoted by Indian Railways as the eco-friendly option (Wikipedia, Kulhar), but they are single-use and fired in coal/wood kilns.
Reusable glass or metal cups create no waste. Paper cups are plastic-lined, plastic glasses are single-use, and kulhads, though biodegradable, use topsoil and kiln fuel each time.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: In Pavlovian conditioning paradigm as developed originally which of the following was used as independent variable?
explanation: In Pavlov's original paradigm the experimenter varied the number of pairings of the conditioned stimulus (bell) with the unconditioned stimulus (food) – the independent variable; response magnitude and latency were the measured (dependent) variables.

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: Who among of the following is not an exponent of Humanistic Realism?
explanation: Humanistic realism is a 16th-century Renaissance school whose exponents were Erasmus, Rabelais and Milton; Aristotle is an ancient Greek philosopher, not one of its exponents. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: Who opined, "The world is continuously evolving towards greater degree of perfection that is God." It is the opinion of
explanation: The idea that the world is continuously evolving towards a greater perfection that is God (the Divine) is Sri Aurobindo's theory of spiritual evolution. Aristotle (the printed key) spoke of an unmoved mover, not of the world evolving into God; Plato and Russell do not hold this view. Off-subject (philosophy of education).

exam: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
q: New ideas (Eureka) suddenly come in the minds of the creative children in which of the following stage?
explanation: In Wallas's stages of creativity (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) the sudden 'Eureka' insight comes at illumination. Off-subject (educational psychology).

exam: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
q: Sum of exterior angles of a convex polygon is
explanation: The exterior angles of any convex polygon, one at each vertex, always add up to 360°. Off-topic (mathematics).
